title: Start and stop a recording
summary: Record a short clip, stop it and open the saved file.

steps.say: Check the preview shows what you want to record. Say next when it looks right.
hints: If the preview is black, add a Display Capture source first.
The lesson called Show your screen with Display Capture walks through it.
steps.why: Whatever is in the preview is what ends up in the file.

steps.say: Click Start Recording in the Controls panel at the bottom right.

checks.prompt: Does the Controls panel now show Stop Recording, with a running timer in the status bar?

hints: It is the second button in the Controls panel, under Start Streaming.
Press Tab until Start Recording is focused, then press Space.
steps.why: Recording only starts when you press this button or a hotkey you set.

steps.say: Let it run for about five seconds. Watch the timer count up in the bottom bar.
hints: The red dot and timer at the bottom show a recording is in progress.
Say next when a few seconds have passed.
steps.why: A short test clip checks picture and sound before a real session.

steps.say: Click Stop Recording in the same place.

checks.prompt: Does the Controls panel show Start Recording again, with the recording timer stopped?

hints: The button changed its text when recording began.
OBS may show a short message with the saved file name.
steps.why: Stopping cleanly finishes the file so every player can open it.

steps.say: Open the File menu and choose Show Recordings to see your new file.

checks.prompt: Is a File Explorer window open showing a folder with a recent video file?

hints: File is the first item in the menu bar at the top left.
Press Alt then F to open the File menu.
steps.why: OBS opens the Recording Path folder so you can play or share the clip.
